answer: An ember dies unless it is tended, so tenure must be re-earned. Each identity must be tended through a tide of audited epochs by two holders outside its own cluster, and one tend serves one identity, so n aliases need n distinct tenders rather than a cooperative ring. Tending an ember costs its depth squared in bond, so the k-th tend an operator claims costs k squared and n heads pay near n cubed. Every claim is carved into a glacier that records its tenders, and an audit re-walks a random groove; an unconfirmed claim melts the whole face and forfeits every bond on it.
